title: ‘Bring Jensen back’: petition passes 150,000 signatures as Huang reportedly weighs a return to Nvidia
summary: The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang kept moving over the weekend, The Verge reported on Sunday, November 15, 2026. A public letter demanding that Nvidia “bring Jensen back” has passed 150,000 signatures, with public support from big names including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, though the signatures are hard to verify: Business Insider found entries such as “Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor” and “Xi Jingping.” The Financial Times reports that Huang has discussed the possibility of returning as CEO with close allies, as some Silicon Valley insiders and employees try to pressure the board. Not everyone agrees; one ally told the FT that “having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offense,” and 23andMe founder Anne Wojcicki told Bloomberg that “power corrupts.” Megaspeed, meanwhile, said Alice Huang left the company effective August 30, 2025, and has no current role there.

title: Congress moves to tighten AI chip export rules after the Nvidia spy scandal
summary: Following the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips, The Verge reported on Sunday, November 15, 2026. Democrats and Republicans have both voiced support for measures and bills that would tighten the rules, and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress, and Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott sent letters to Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling on them to testify publicly. Bills such as the Remote Access Security Act, first introduced in the House in April 2025 but stalled in the Senate, are getting renewed interest. House Speaker Mike Johnson said there is “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China,” according to Reuters.

title: Apple launches a study app to learn how people use AI for health questions
summary: Apple is partnering with healthcare AI company OpenEvidence on a new study app to understand how people use AI for health, TechCrunch reported on Sunday, November 15, 2026. The study is open to U.S. users over 21 with an iPhone 15 or later running iOS 26 or later with Apple Intelligence enabled, and Apple aims to enroll up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months. Participants can ask health questions and get simplified answers grounded in clinical sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, the Journal of the American Medical Association and Nature, rate the answers and take monthly surveys. They can share HealthKit data such as resting heart rate, sleep or lab results for more personal suggestions, and the app can help prepare for a doctor’s visit. Apple said the data will be anonymized and won’t be used to train AI models, and OpenEvidence deletes query and response data after 24 hours.

title: OpenAI opens a science blog with a physicist’s GPT-6 Astra–assisted lattice definition of the Standard Model
summary: OpenAI launched a separate science blog on Sunday, November 15, 2026, with a guest post by physicist Nathaniel Craig of the University of California, Santa Barbara, describing a candidate non-perturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model of particle physics built in collaboration with the GPT-6 Astra model, mlllm.io reported. An accompanying preprint is on arXiv and was reviewed by lattice specialists Maarten Golterman, Andreas Kronfeld and Yigal Shamir. According to Craig, the model proposed the method for transferring fields to finer lattices and demonstrated convergence of the comparisons. Chiral theories like the Standard Model have resisted a rigorous lattice definition for decades. If the community confirms the construction, mlllm.io notes, it would set a precedent for AI-accelerated proofs in mathematical physics.

title: S&P 500 futures slip into a week built around Nvidia’s results and Anthropic’s IPO
summary: U.S. stock futures fell Monday morning, November 16, 2026, dragged down by technology stocks, as traders awaited Nvidia’s earnings and a potentially record-setting public debut by Anthropic this week, CNBC reported. S&P 500 futures fell 0.7% and Nasdaq-100 futures declined 1.5%, while Dow futures shed 55 points, or 0.1%. Chipmakers Micron, Intel and AMD each lost more than 5% in premarket trading, Dell also fell more than 5%, and Oracle slipped nearly 4%. Wall Street is coming off a winning week despite Nvidia’s tumble: the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted their biggest weekly gains since August, rising more than 2% each. Overseas, Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.42% after third-quarter GDP unexpectedly shrank, and South Korea’s Kospi slumped 3.59%.

title: Nvidia faces its first earnings test without Huang after a week that wiped out more than $500 billion
summary: Nvidia shares plunged more than 12% last week, wiping out over $500 billion in value and pushing the company’s market capitalization below $4 trillion for the first time since 2025 after long-time CEO Jensen Huang was ousted, Investing.com reported on Monday, November 16, 2026. Traders are now gearing up for Nvidia’s fiscal third-quarter results after the market close on Tuesday. Analysts at Vital Knowledge said they will watch whether Nvidia reiterates its forecast for 70% annual growth in its next fiscal year, and warned investors to focus on the potential for Washington to dramatically strengthen AI chip export rules. JPMorgan analysts said clarity on future leadership will be critical, especially after reports of support for a movement to return Huang to the company.

title: Anthropic’s IPO arrives this week as the AI giant eyes a roughly $1.4 trillion valuation
summary: Anthropic’s initial public offering is another key test for the AI trade this week, CNBC reported Monday, November 16, 2026, with the company eyeing a roughly $1.4 trillion valuation and shares expected to be priced between $70 and $78. The listing comes as AI-linked stocks slid in premarket trading ahead of Nvidia’s results. Investing.com described the debut of the Claude chatbot maker as a possible signal that the AI boom is moving from a picks-and-shovels phase to one where these tools are harnessed to create lucrative products. Shares of Anthropic are not yet trading.

title: Micron ends a 12.8% weekly gain at $778.31 as memory waits on Nvidia’s numbers
summary: Micron closed at $778.31 on Friday, November 13, 2026, down 2.52% on the day but up about 12.8% for the week, Chip Dispatch reported on Sunday. Most of the weekly move came Wednesday, when shares jumped 11.89% after CoreWeave raised its outlook and said its capacity was largely sold out through 2027. Micron fell 1.59% Thursday and 2.52% Friday after Nvidia said Jensen Huang had resigned, holding up better than Sandisk, and the stock still sits about 21% below its October 28 close. No Micron-specific news emerged over the weekend. Nvidia, which buys Micron’s high-bandwidth memory, reports Tuesday, November 17, and its data center numbers, fiscal 2028 outlook and Vera Rubin supply are the items that matter most for Micron, the report said.

title: Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter model that cuts per-task cost by 62%
summary: Alibaba on Monday, November 16, 2026, released Qwen4-Max, the first flagship model on its new Qwen4 architecture, mlllm.io reported. It uses a mixture-of-experts backbone with 2.4 trillion parameters, 71 billion of them active per token, accepts text, images and video, and handles contexts of up to 1 million tokens. New attention components include Gated DeltaNet, Qwen Sparse Attention and Gated Residual. On Alibaba’s internal Work360 benchmark, Qwen4-Max scored 52.69 versus 47.74 for Qwen3.8-Max, and the average cost per task fell from $4.43 to $1.67, according to the vendor’s own data. API prices are $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens. It is available via QwenCloud, Qwen Studio, QwenWork and Qoder; the weights are closed, though Alibaba promises to open smaller Qwen4 models later.

title: Tencent’s Hy4 flash is a budget model built to make everyday AI tasks cheap
summary: Tencent on November 16, 2026, introduced Hy4 flash, a budget tier of its Hy4 lineup for everyday work tasks, mlllm.io reported. It is a 224-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 12 billion parameters active per token, including 64 billion parameters for an Engram conditional memory. It is natively multimodal, supports up to 1 million tokens of context and generates text at over 150 tokens per second. API rates are $0.070 per million input tokens and $0.281 per million output tokens, versus $0.834 and $2.501 for the flagship Hy4. In Tencent’s own blind test of 85 WorkBuddy users across 259 tasks, satisfaction was comparable to Claude Haiku 5.5; mlllm.io notes these are vendor figures. Tencent says the model lags in complex programming and long agent tasks. It is free to try in WorkBuddy until November 30.

title: Edge0 opens 145B and 120B models meant to run on consumer Nvidia GPUs, with license limits
summary: Edge0 has published 145-billion- and 120-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model variants, extending its local-inference effort beyond earlier 35B and 8B releases, Open Model Weights reported on Sunday, November 15, 2026. The models are derivatives of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next rather than independently trained foundation models. The 145B card lists 10.12 billion active parameters per token, a 256K context configuration and a 40.81 GiB weight package, and Edge0 reports 121.2 agent-decode tokens per second on an RTX 5090 D 24 GB; Open Model Weights notes these are publisher measurements, not its own reproductions. A 24 GB GPU does not hold the larger weight set alone, so the project streams experts from system RAM. Supported builds point to Linux or Windows, an Nvidia GPU, CUDA 13 and Edge0’s own inference engine.

title: MIT’s Automatar bass guitar hides an AI computer that plays harmony on its own strings
summary: Antonis Christou, a researcher in the MIT Media Lab’s Opera of the Future group, presented Automatar, a bass guitar with an Nvidia Jetson Orin NX module embedded in its body, mlllm.io reported on Monday, November 16, 2026. The musician plays four main strings while a locally running AI model analyzes the performance and electromagnetically vibrates five additional strings, building harmony on the fly. The signal chain runs through a Bela Mini with SuperCollider, converts each string to MIDI, and the model generates sine waves that excite the extra strings through high-voltage amplifiers. The body is built from Pale Moon Ebony and mahogany, combining traditional luthier work with CNC milling and 3D printing. It is a research prototype, not a product, and a rare case of AI answering through the mechanics of strings rather than a screen.

title: Bharat Semi raises $24 million to put AI and vision on a single image-sensor chip
summary: Indian semiconductor startup Bharat Semi has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors, TechCrunch reported on Sunday, November 15, 2026. The New Delhi-based company is building programmable sensors that combine image capture, processing and AI on one chip, which co-founder Vrinda Kapoor says could cut system costs by at least 70% compared with setups that use a separate sensor, image processor and system-on-chip. “Our aim here is to move from sensors to sense-making solutions,” Kapoor said. The pre-revenue startup reports design wins with General Atomics and India’s Kaynes Semicon and targets initial commercial production in 2027. Uses include air conditioners that detect an empty room and drones that process what they see. The round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures.

title: Freshworks alums raise $53 million for Dreamteam, an AI-native CRM with a ‘Company Brain’
summary: Dreamteam, founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to challenge Salesforce and HubSpot with an AI-native CRM, TechCrunch reported on Monday, November 16, 2026. The seed and Series A rounds were led by Together Fund and Accel, with Premji Invest participating. Instead of relying on salespeople to log every interaction, Dreamteam captures context from emails and customer conversations into what it calls the Company Brain, and four built-in AI agents research prospects, draft follow-ups, flag deal risks and configure workflows, with teams keeping control over what gets sent. The startup says it signed more than 100 customers across 13 countries in three months of selling. “We see this as an electric-car moment for systems of record,” said CEO Anand Venkatraman. It aims for eight figures in annual revenue by the end of 2027.

title: A New Jersey teen taught himself machine learning to build Kora, a free app helping families read autistic children’s cues
summary: New Jersey high schooler Shashank Madala watched adults who loved his autistic younger cousin guess, often wrongly, at why he was upset at family gatherings, Good News Network reported. At 15, with a single computer science class behind him, Madala taught himself machine learning and built Kora, a free app that offers caregivers several possible readings of what an autistic child may be feeling, with no scores, diagnoses or judgments. Early versions gave one fast, confident answer; he rebuilt it to slow adults down and to flag when it is unsure, leaving the final judgment to the adult who knows the child. Kora now has more than 700 users in 12 countries and won the Congressional App Challenge for New Jersey’s 10th District. “If you are looking for something that matters, it is probably already in your house,” he said.

title: Students inspired by a father’s three heart attacks win Bangladesh’s FutureMakers with an AI stethoscope clip
summary: A teammate’s experience with her father’s three heart attacks led a group of university students to build EchoClip, an AI-powered device that attaches to a conventional stethoscope and analyzes heart sounds for early signs of heart disease, The Daily Star reported on Monday, November 16, 2026. The team, LubDub, with students from the University of Dhaka, Bangladesh University of Professionals and BRAC University, won the championship at Grameenphone’s FutureMakers 2026 competition in Dhaka on November 10. They trained their model on more than 10,000 publicly available heart recordings. Runners-up built an AI river-erosion prediction system, inspired by a member who saw families displaced from their homes, and Spasto AI, a speech therapy app. Held under the theme “AI for Social Good,” the competition drew more than 7,000 students and 1,103 ideas from over 70 universities.

title: #LafayetteBuiltThis invites anyone to build their own small app tonight, no coding needed
summary: #LafayetteBuiltThis, a hands-on community build night, takes place today, Monday, November 16, from 5 to 8 p.m. at 314 Jefferson St. in downtown Lafayette, according to the event’s One Acadiana community calendar listing. Neighbors, friends, families and CGI experts will spend the evening building small, useful, personal things together, such as a recipe website, a family photo organizer, a homework helper, a small-business inventory tracker or a bedtime-story generator for kids. You do not need to be technical or know how to code; patient human helpers will sit with you, explain each step in plain language and help whenever you get stuck. The event is hosted by CGI, Opportunity Machine and the Lafayette Regional Technology Council.

title: Teens can make pumpkin string art at the Main Library tonight
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s Main Library, 301 W. Congress St., hosts Pumpkin String Art today, Monday, November 16, from 6 to 7 p.m., according to the library’s event listing. The in-person program, held in the first-floor Teen conference room, invites participants to craft a decorative pumpkin from wood, nails and string to take home and display all autumn. It is for ages 12 to 18, and registration is required, with a limited number of seats.

title: Collage your own flyers for Acadiana’s community art zine Wednesday at the AcA
summary: The Acadiana Center for the Arts, 101 W. Vermilion St., hosts Artist Round Up: Collaging, Flyer Making, and the Community Zine on Wednesday, November 18, from 6 to 8 p.m., according to the AcA’s event page, with an RSVP. Former Artist Alliance member Jesse Poimboeuf leads a night of collaging and mixed-media artmaking as participants put together the 7th issue of the Creative Acadiana Community Art Zine. Inspired by the grassroots flyers the Artist Alliance made by hand in the ’90s, you’ll collage flyers of your own, for real events, fake events, concepts or anything you can imagine. Collaging materials and scissors are provided, and you’re encouraged to bring old photos, stickers and patterned paper. Creatives of all levels are welcome.

title: Twenty Years of Valcour Records brings C.J. Chenier, Wayne Toups and more to the AcA Thursday
summary: The Acadiana Center for the Arts’ James Devin Moncus Theater, 101 W. Vermilion St., hosts Twenty Years of Valcour Records on Thursday, November 19, from 7:30 to 9:30 p.m., according to the AcA’s event page. Tickets are listed at $40. Founded in Eunice by Joel Savoy and Phillip LaFargue, Valcour has spent two decades preserving Cajun, Creole, zydeco and folk traditions, and this Louisiana Crossroads concert brings together the label’s musicians and collaborators to trace its path from friends recording in Savoy’s living room to a nationally respected label. The lineup includes C.J. Chenier, T’Monde, the Pine Leaf Boys, The Band Courtbouillon featuring Wayne Toups, the Mamou Playboys, Jourdan Thibodeaux, Bonsoir Catin, Ann Savoy, Joel Savoy and many more.

title: Accidental Astronauts takes kids on a planetarium trip to the Moon Saturday at the Lafayette Science Museum
summary: The Lafayette Science Museum, 433 Jefferson St., shows Accidental Astronauts in its planetarium on Saturday, November 21, from 11:15 a.m. to noon, according to the museum’s event listing, which places it among its kids’ special programs. The show follows Cy and Annie and their dog Armstrong on an unexpected journey into space with a wise-cracking spaceship computer. Along the way, audiences explore the Earth, Sun and Moon system, see an asteroid crash into the Moon, bounce along the lunar surface and get up close to a solar storm. The museum calls it a space adventure for all ages.

title: Geno Delafose brings zydeco to Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette Sunday evening
summary: Zydeco musician Geno Delafose plays Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette, 905 Jefferson St., on Sunday, November 22, at 5 p.m., according to the venue’s event page, which lists the act as a zydeco band. Tickets are listed at $17 plus a $0.43 ticket service fee. Anyone under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. The early-evening start makes it an easy way to close out the weekend before Thanksgiving week with live zydeco.
